inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 757.252m issued at 30 June 2026 plus 4.356m performance rights (FY26 AR EPS note, 761.376m weighted diluted). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, DRP suspended, no buybacks.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR cash-flow reconciliation, share-based payments expense $4,180k (RRL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:7005); equity-award cash taxes nil (net-share settlement not used)
inputs.gold_price_anchor: Spot US$4,304/oz (GC=F) at AUDUSD 0.7016 = ~A$6,135/oz on 2026-09-25; FY26 realised A$6,283/oz unhedged; 30-Jun-26 spot A$5,861/oz; 3yr realised average A$4,549, 5yr A$3,689; McPhillamys PFS deck A$4,000/oz
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built rate: ACGB 10yr ~4.4% + 0.95 beta x 5.5% ERP = ~9.6% cost of equity; zero debt so WACC = CoE, rounded to 9.5%. One rate for all three scenarios: gold-price cyclicality, reserve-life and McPhillamys permitting risk are charged in the flows and the scenario weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. FY26 lease principal $18.7m (financing) + lease interest $7.457m (operating) = $26.2m = 1.1% of revenue charged via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities ($101.7m) EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct_path is ex right-of-use depreciation (~$20m/yr) so the lease is not charged twice in the tax line.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Tropicana (30%) is an unincorporated joint venture proportionately consolidated; no non-controlling interest exists in the FY26 accounts.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the cyclical adaptations. Regis is a pure-play, unhedged, debt-free Australian gold producer (Duketon 100%, Tropicana 30%) whose revenue is ounces x gold price, so the growth_rates path IS a gold-price path on a flat-to-declining ounce profile, not a business growth rate. MID-CYCLE, NOT PEAK: FY26 realised A$6,283/oz and spot A$6,135/oz are record highs (~2x the global 90th-percentile AISC); the base case normalises the realised price to A$5,000/oz by FY29 (FY27 5,900, FY28 5,400) and escalates 2%/yr thereafter, with unit cash costs (AISC less sustaining capex, A$2,700/oz in FY26) at A$2,850 in FY27 rising 3%/yr to FY30 and 2.5%/yr after. Production: FY27 guidance 360-400koz (17-Jul-26 release) taken at the 380koz midpoint, drifting to 360koz as Duketon open pits deplete and the underground strategy (target 200-250koz Duketon + 120-145koz Tropicana attributable) sustains the rest. Ore Reserves ex-McPhillamys are ~2.0Moz attributable (~5.5 years) but Regis has replaced underground reserves six years running; the terminal is capped at 12x owner FCF (bull 14x, bear 8x) because the asset depletes. Capex path is total investing cash (sustaining ~$250/oz + underground development + exploration ~$75m), FY26 $440.7m tapering to ~$310-330m by FY29 as Garden Well Main/Rosemont Stage 3/BuckWell complete; growth capital that sustains 360koz is treated as required, not optional. Interest income stripped (net cash $1,139m > 1x FCF base). BRIDGE items not in the flows: -$246.5m current tax payable at 30-Jun-26 (FY26 tax paid in FY27; forward tax is charged at 30% on forward EBIT), -$151.5m final 15c + special 5c dividend declared 20-Aug-26 with record date 11-Sep-26 (price is ex-dividend, cash leaves 7-Oct-26), -$178.0m rehabilitation provision (non-current, at PV; closure spend sits beyond the horizon), +$400m risked McPhillamys (35% x PFS NPV5.5% of $1.13bn at A$4,000/oz; project blocked by the Section 10 declaration, Federal Court judgment reserved since Dec-25, FID for the IWL alternative targeted H1 CY2028, $1.08bn pre-production capex). McPhillamys is EXCLUDED from all three flow paths; at spot gold its unrisked NPV would be several times the bridge value, which makes the bull conservative on this axis. FY27 AISC/capex guidance from the 17-Jul-26 release was not in the extracted filings; year-1 costs are anchored on FY26 actuals plus the disclosed diesel and BuckWell open-pit pressure (implied FY27 AISC ~A$3,100/oz). Analysis JSON not yet available at build time; qualitative context from the FY26 annual report.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: long-run nominal gold-price escalation on flat ounces; historical CAGRs are gold-price artefacts, not a growth trend
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.6% vs revenue 23.5% and EPS 29.1%: the divergence is the gold price (A$2,229/oz FY21 -> A$6,283/oz FY26, +23%/yr) on ~flat ounces (367koz -> 374koz sold), plus the FY21 Tropicana acquisition ($885m, equity raise 509m -> 755m shares). None of these CAGRs is a forward growth rate.
historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal (treatment B): FY16 115.2, FY17 95.8, FY18 138.6, FY19 83.6, FY20 104.9, FY21 48.8, FY22 -7.0, FY23 19.2, FY24 162.9, FY25 510.3, FY26 753.8 (A$m). EPS 3yr CAGR undefined (FY23 EPS -0.032 after Tropicana stamp duty and FY24 -0.246 after the $193.5m impairment and $97.7m hedge buyout). FY22-24 owner FCF was near zero at A$2,300-3,000/oz gold with $300m+ development capex: that is what the bear case looks like.

base.narrative: Existing operations at a normalised gold price. FY27 at the 380koz guidance midpoint with gold still near spot, then a two-year mean reversion to A$5,000/oz (above the 3-year realised average of A$4,549 and the A$4,000 McPhillamys PFS deck, ~18% below spot). Duketon open pits deplete and the underground mines (Garden Well, Rosemont, Garden Well Main, Havana at Tropicana) hold group output near 360koz. Capex stays near D&A because the underground growth capital is what sustains the ounces. Terminal capped at 12x owner FCF: a depleting asset with ~5.5 years of ex-McPhillamys reserves and a six-year record of replacing them.

bull.gold_price_path_note: Realised A$/oz: FY27 6,200, FY28 6,350, FY29 6,500, then +2.5%/yr (FY36 7,727). Ounces sold: 385, 395, 400 then 400koz flat as the fourth Duketon underground and Havana ramp up. Same unit cost path as base. Capex A$m ~400, 380, 350 then ~13.3% of revenue.
bull.narrative: Gold holds its record real level and drifts up with inflation; central-bank buying and fiscal debasement keep the price near A$6,200-6,500 through FY29. Regis reaches its stated aspiration of four underground mines at Duketon plus Havana at Tropicana, lifting group output to 400koz, and reserve replacement continues. Capex intensity falls as the FY26-27 development wave completes. McPhillamys remains at the same risked bridge value, so this case is conservative on that axis even though at these prices the unrisked NPV would exceed $2bn.

bear.gold_price_path_note: Realised A$/oz: FY27 5,500, FY28 4,600, FY29 4,200, FY30 4,200, then +2%/yr (FY36 4,730). Ounces sold: 365, 355, 345, 340, 335, 330, 325, 320, 315, 310 koz as reserve replacement falters. Unit cash cost A$/oz 2,900 rising 3.5%/yr to FY30 then 2.5%/yr (FY36 3,729). Capex cut to committed projects then sustaining plus minimal development (~$210m/yr).
bear.narrative: Gold mean-reverts hard, as it did after 2011: realised price back to A$4,200/oz by FY29 (the McPhillamys PFS deck; FY25 realised A$4,387) while Australian mining costs keep inflating with diesel, labour and the BuckWell open-pit restart. Underground reserve replacement slows, open pits at Duketon run out and group output slides toward 310koz. Management cuts growth capital, which protects near-term cash but shortens mine life; owner FCF falls toward the FY22-24 experience of near-zero. The cash pile, tax payable, dividend and rehab bridge are then most of the value.

scenario_narratives.base: Normalised gold (A$5,000/oz by FY29, +2%/yr after) on ~360-380koz from Duketon and 30% of Tropicana, unit costs escalating 2.5-3%/yr, capex near D&A to sustain the underground strategy, terminal capped at 12x owner FCF for a depleting asset. McPhillamys carried only as a 35%-risked bridge item.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold holds record levels (A$6,200-6,500/oz, +2.5%/yr), Regis reaches four Duketon undergrounds plus Havana for 400koz, capex intensity falls as the FY26-27 development wave completes; terminal 14x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Gold reverts to A$4,200/oz by FY29 while costs inflate 3.5%/yr; reserve replacement falters and output slides to 310koz; growth capital is cut; owner FCF returns to the near-zero FY22-24 range and the balance sheet is most of the value; terminal 8x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25% because the single dominant driver, the gold price, sits at a record ~2x the industry's marginal cost with no hedging, and FY22-24 showed this exact asset base producing near-zero owner FCF at A$2,300-3,000/oz. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to hold: gold staying at record real levels for a decade AND the underground growth to 400koz with continued reserve replacement. Base 50%: the balance sheet (debt-free, $1.1bn cash) removes solvency risk from every path, so the weights are about the price deck, not survival.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the existing Duketon and Tropicana ounces at a normalised, not peak, gold price; charge the growth capital that sustains production as a real cost; count the cash pile once (interest income stripped) and net it against the liabilities the 30-June balance sheet has not yet paid (FY26 tax, declared dividend, rehabilitation); carry McPhillamys as a risked option rather than in the flows; cap the terminal because the asset depletes. Risk is charged in the flows and scenario weights, once, at a single AUD-built 9.5% WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price: every A$500/oz on 370koz is ~A$185m of pre-tax cash flow (~A$0.17/share of annual owner FCF, several dollars of value). The base deck (A$5,000 by FY29) is a judgment; spot is A$6,135 and the 3-year realised average A$4,549.

Reserve life: ex-McPhillamys reserves ~2.0Moz attributable (~5.5 years). The 12x terminal cap assumes replacement continues as it has for six years; if it stops the terminal is too high and the bear ounce profile is the base.

Cost inflation: FY26 AISC rose 16% to $2,945/oz on diesel and the Duketon North restart; the paths escalate costs faster than price in the base case, and any AISC step-change above A$3,300/oz compresses the margin further.

McPhillamys permitting: the $400m bridge is a 35% probability on a A$4,000/oz PFS. An adverse Federal Court ruling plus IWL approval failure takes it to zero (-$0.53/share); a clean approval at spot gold could be worth $2bn+ unrisked.

Capex classification: the model treats underground development capital as required to hold ounces flat. If management can hold 360koz on materially less capital than the FY22-26 average, the base is too low.
FY27 guidance for AISC and capex from the 17-Jul-26 release was not in the extracted filings; year-1 costs are inferred from FY26 actuals and should be checked against the September 2026 quarterly.
